Ok I'm here to leave a very clear review...this is a stunning trail. It is dog friendly BUT when you are near the trailhead (we parked at 10th line) you will be absolutely bombarded with huge groups of people very spread out with absolutely no trail manners whatsoever. You'll spend what feels like an eternity pulled over to the side waiting for these huge families to pass you. Of course you could try to avoid busy times but anytime the weather and conditions are right this will occur. Go counter clockwise with dogs so that you are going up the ladder. It's not steep so you can carry or pass a small dog to the top and larger dogs can handle going up the rocks to the left of the ladder. There are NO cattle ladders on this map. The person that posted that here must have been on a different route. There's no scrambling and it is not "difficult" for an experienced hiker. Anything less than experienced should not be completing a 12km loop. And it is 12.1km. We did it in 3hrs 10 minutes moving time with at least 15minss spent waitingggggggg for people to walk past us and our dogs.

A few notes if you're planning to do it in winter. First, the road is closed in Winter that leads to the parking location that is loaded in Alltrails. I parked on the lot which is on 10th line instead. Then the main issue you'll run into is that parts of this loop are on cross country ski trails. Not a problem this year as there's not enough snow for skiing, but beware that you won't be able to do this loop if the ski trails are up and running. You can still do a great hike, but you'd have to modify the route a bit.  The trail was slippery throughout and icy in places. Use trail crampons. Lots of up and down, and lots of crazy cracks and crevices. The part of the trail on the East side of 10th Line is the most technical part of the trail (there's even a ladder), so if that's not your cup of tea, then take the road and skip that part of the trail. All in all it was awesome, it's got a waterfall, a river gorge walk, several forest types, and awesome vistas.

Very well marked and beautiful hike. Moderate due to length easy to moderate for anyone.

What an amazing day! Unseasonably warm… it got to 24C.l! Arrived at the trailhead around 9am, with only a a few people parked there, but when we got back the road was lined up with many cars. Really great

Nice moderate hike with hard spots along the way. Most of the hike is in the forest in shade but some open areas. I was fine with bud spray, didn’t get bothered much. (Again I started the trail by going right at the first Y) most the good views and the waterfall were in the first 5k. 
Great day! My phone says I hiked just over 11km.
Beautiful!! We did half the trail from the start to the bridge and back (~8.5k). The lookout is awesome!! Some areas were very muddy though because of the rain yesterday.

Great views, don't go when it's wet

Amazing!

Great variety of stuff from lookouts, caverns, good climbs and wonderful waterfalls... give yourself enough time.  And, if it just rained it will be slippery.  Would I call it difficult, BC is difficult but this has some great stuff in it if you are looking for variety in a day hike.  Its a good hike for sure.  I would do it again.  Careful of parking it is limited, park off of country road 9.

A bit muddy

good

Great Trail with variety of grasslands, roots and rocks. Some Rocky areas tricky but doable. Great vistas, Caves & crevices to enjoy.

Great! Extremely beautiful. Very challenging at parts for me because it was over 30 today. Lots and lots of creeks and streams to cool down at for myself and the dogs. Very buggy. Bring bug spray. Switching between following the white or blue swatches/blazes can be a bit confusing at times. But use the app and it'll keep you out of trouble. Otherwise it is a well marked trail.

Pretty even effort to reward ratio. So good overall

awesome hike, lots of variation and some challenge… it’ll push ya at times but super fun overall

We did veer off in the wrong direction a few times, but we had the map loaded up through all trails ap, so we just kept checking to make sure we were on approximately the same route. I think we cut a few corners as our trip was a couple km less than most peoples. Most people out today had snow shoes, cross country skiis or crampons. Probably do this trail again in the spring!

one of the best hikes around, varied terrain, water, cliffs and caves/crevices.  challenge with the soft ground and inclines.  about 4 hours are a relaxed pace.

Fun route on the Bruce Trail! Caves were really cool and it was only occasionally muddy.

Great trail. After rains and in assuming in the spring you will definitely need to be prepared for mud. Bring proper gear. Note sections that are closed during certain times of the year. My assumption is that it's for hunting on private property.

My favorite hike now in Ontario!
Quite busy but very nice trail, we lost the turn somehow and ended up hiking shorter loop, watch the marking carefully.
Great trail. Was slippery and muddy due to rain night before.

I would consider this a hard trail with some very challenging portions, but still beautiful and worth the effort required! Very muddy and occasionally downright dangerous! Markers are good for the most part, except at the very end, where it got confusing.

If you don't want to read my whole review, I'll sum it up. It's gorgeous and has everything you want in a hike, but it is HARD. This particular loop that AllTrails suggests is not an easy hike and I would not recommend it at all for beginners or people without proper gear. 

The beginning of this trail has some fairly technical bits, but you have a lot of energy at the beginning, so it's not too bad. The middle is the most scenic bit and definitely my favourite part and it's a good workout. There's some lovely lookout points and a waterfall. It's very muddy in parts, so be extra careful and take your time.

However, the ending was VERY HARD. I would not rate this section as just "moderate". At this point, I had already walked for about 4 hours so I was pretty tired, so having to navigate through steep inclines, narrow paths, and big rocks was incredibly challenging.

I also ended up getting lost at the very end as the AllTrails map is pretty confusing and the blazes aren't very clear. However, other then this, the trail was actually very well marked and easy to follow. 

I had the middle bit of the hike completely to myself, it was incredibly tranquil and I felt like I was really in the middle of the woods. The beginning and end were a bit busier, but not horrendous. I did get to the parking lot at the same time as a large hiking club, but I never ended up encountering them on the trail. 

I also never saw any caves. 

Overall, I would suggest this trail to a more experienced hiker. 

Make sure you know what you're getting yourself into.

parking conditions are horrible.  There are about 6 parking spaces and then dozens of cars on the road. We got a $50 parking ticket for obstructing traffic. Seems like a money grab by the municipality as there is still plenty of room for cars to travel on the road with a line of cars on one side.

3rd time here. Still love this trail due to various terrains.

Ok so this trail is AWESOME!!! It actually ended up being a little over 11km for me, but I want to point out that you can hike Duncan caves in a much shorter distance. This particular trail set up to start you at Duncan caves and takes you off Provincial land via the Bruce trail (you don’t have to do this if you’re worried this is too long!!). However if you decide to do it all, it’s worth it! This trail takes you past crevices, waterfalls, rivers, forest stands, and meadows! Such a diversity of sights. One of my fav trails so far. Lots of variety. Never a dull moment. Beautiful views.

Pay close attention to your GPS once you hit the Metcalfe Side Trail/Kolapore Uplands parking lot, it’s easy to get turned around here. We completed the trail counter clockwise as suggested by others and it was perfect!  Definitely parts that were moderate difficulty. 4 hours to complete with stops for sightseeing and lunch.
was fairly buggy but it didn't bother me too much, lots of shade some suprising rock climbing parts were fun
Great trail with a variety of scenery! From looks over the escarpment to walking bridges over the rivers/creeks. Beautiful trail at moderate difficulty.
Crevices and side trails worth exploring! Main trail was well kept, and some well built creek crossings provided a nice place to stop.
Great trail,amazing hike! We took our 7 year old and he loved it so much! Especially the crevice caves. Will definitely be visiting again!!

This is an extremely beautiful trail with varied terrain.  Hiking shoes are absolutely required to navigate a few sections.  It is definitely “moderate”.  I echo the comment about doing the loop counter-clockwise (ie follow the Bruce Trail white blaze markings) unless you want to incorporate more cardio.  Regardless you won’t be disappointed.
A good hike. The ground was damp following overnight rain, combined with fallen leaves, meant footing in some places was slippery.

Beautiful day for a hike. Signage at Metcalf was very poor and a few other areas after.  Shortly after there is a bit of a ladder that was slightly difficult for my dog. 
Parking lot holds about 5 cars but can park on roadside. 
Energetic hike took 4 hours including rest and getting turned around.
Need good shoes lots of rocks.
Great hiking spot. Diverse landscapes, beautiful views. Bugs were not bad at all. Would definitely explore this area again.
Sept 15 - very warm day for hiking but the cedar and delicious tree canopy made for a very comfortable hike.  Amazing crevices!
Went with a friend and her baby in a hiking carrier. We switched back and forth on the trail. It slowed us down but was still a great hike.

Turn right to take the trail counter clockwise as you will be doing most of the harder parts of the trail on a decline.  Catch the Bluffs first and around to the caves. Some tougher terrain but absolutely outstanding trail!  100% recommend
A great summer day for a hike.   This is a moderate trail with numerous elevation changes.  Bring bug spray.  This is some of the nicest scenery in this section of the Bruce Trail.

This is primarily an easy to moderate trail. We were there in on long weekend and hardly saw any other hikers which was nice. It is quite beautiful with changing scenery from Deepwoods to rocks to open fields. I would recommend it if you have a wide variety of levels in your group.

Hiked Duncan Caves Trail. Would agree this trail is moderate difficulty. Lots of steep inclines and declines. Lots of rocks and roots along the trail. Walking through the cave is cool, the temperature even drops. Very busy trail. However, could just be because it was a long weekend.
The Metcalfe Crevice side trail was the highlight.
Very lightly trafficked with tones of to explore.

For someone new to hiking this trail route was a challenge but enjoyable. At my beginner pace it took 3:15hr including a lunch at the top and going off route about 1km to go through the caves etc. I got a bit turned around at the escarpment because the many other forks and paths aren’t in the map so pay close attention to your gps for guidance in this area. Beautiful views and a great afternoon !

Great very lightly trafficked trail. Nice mix of flat, hills and rock areas to climb, also has multiple water crossings (great for the dogs). As others have said I highly recommend doing the hike counterclockwise, otherwise you will be hiking up quite a few inclines. Overall great day out, would do it again.

if you come in from the Collingwood side of 9th line the winter maintenance on this road stops About 2 km from the parking lot with a large snowbank blocking the road so you cant access the parking lot.
would recommend going counter clockwise. good views, great water features and rock scrambles. pretty easy - flat enough in most parts to be a trail run. i'd never seen the ladders before. very cool!
Beautiful views. Got lost a bit tho!
Make sure you follow the yellow tags or you will go the wrong way!! After the zig zag bridge turn right!!!!

A great hike. I chose a side trail at one point that involved climbing some rocks - favourite part of the hike. A lot of running water to enjoy listening to. Would like to do it again in the summer. 

My phone died and stopped the recording but it ended up being about 10km.
Great walk!  Easy to follow signs and route on the app was close to actual.

We began our hike at the parking lot. Ok. Where else.
Our hike was very enjoyable until we got into the escarpment part BLUE trail(about 5km later) and we lost our way. 
We are new to hiking but the directions to follow are not that difficult. We went back and forth to find markers.
Finally we decided to take the road back to the car, because it was the shortst way possible at this point.
I'd love to do the trail again
Kind of disappointing.  No caves?
